questions.subtopic: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the grammatically correct auxiliary verb:
"The complete list of all candidates shortlisted for the technical interview ___ uploaded on the High Court notice board."
questions.explanation: Sentence ka grammatical subject 'The complete list' (singular head noun) hai. 'of all candidates shortlisted...' ek prepositional phrase hai jo preposition 'of' se shuru ho raha hai; 'candidates' preposition ka object hai. Singular head noun 'list' ke hisaab se singular auxiliary 'has been' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.hint: Preposition 'of' ke baad aane wale plural noun 'candidates' ko ignore karein. Sentence kiske baare mein hai—candidates ke baare mein ya list ke baare mein?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence:
"The Chief Justice, along with three senior judges, ___ scheduled to address the judicial academy tomorrow."
questions.explanation: 'Along with' coordinate conjunction ('and') nahi hai; ye ek parenthetical phrase hai jo additional information deta hai. Subject-Verb agreement strictly FIRST SUBJECT ('The Chief Justice' [singular]) ke hisaab se decide hota hai. Isliye singular verb 'is' correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Parenthetical Connectives & The First-Subject Rule
questions.hint: 'Along with three senior judges' ko brackets mein rakhkar dekhein. Sentence ka actual subject sirf 'The Chief Justice' hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank:
"Neither the Section Officer nor the computer operators ___ able to restore the damaged database before midnight."
questions.explanation: 'Neither ... nor' construction mein Proximity Rule (Rule of Nearness) lagta hai. Verb apne physically nearest subject ke number se agree karti hai. Verb position ke sabse paas 'the computer operators' (plural noun) hai, isliye plural past auxiliary 'were' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Correlative Conjunctions & The Proximity Rule
questions.hint: Check karein ki verb ke sabse paas kaun sa subject hai: 'Section Officer' (singular) ya 'computer operators' (plural)?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Identify the grammatically correct auxiliary verb:
"Each of the newly installed courtroom microphones ___ tested by the sound engineer this morning."
questions.explanation: 'Each of + plural noun' construction mein true subject distributive pronoun 'EACH' hota hai jo hamesha singular hota hai. 'Microphones' preposition 'of' ka plural object hai. Singular subject 'Each' ke hisaab se singular verb 'was' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Distributive Singular Pronouns: Each, Every, Either of, Neither of
questions.hint: 'Microphones' plural dekhkar attract na hon. Subject 'Each' hai jo hamesha singular verb leta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: 'A Number of' vs 'The Number of' Concord
questions.question:
Choose the option that correctly completes the statement:
"___ of cyber security complaints received by the registry has increased dramatically over the last quarter."
questions.explanation: Sentence mein aage finite verb 'HAS increased' (singular) aayi hai. 'A number of' ke sath plural verb lagti hai ('have increased'), jabki 'The number of' ek specific single numerical figure denote karta hai aur singular verb ('has increased') leta hai. Isliye 'The number' hi grammatically valid hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: 'A Number of' (Plural) vs 'The Number of' (Singular)
questions.hint: Verb dekhein—sentence mein 'HAS' laga hai. Kaun sa phrase singular verb demand karta hai: 'A number of' ya 'The number of'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: Relative Clause Antecedent Concord: 'One of those who...'
questions.question:
Identify the option with the correct verb concord:
"Pooja is one of those dedicated stenographers who ___ capable of typing exceeding eighty words per minute."
questions.explanation: In 'One of those [Plural Noun] who...', relative pronoun 'who' ka antecedent uske theek pehle aane wala plural noun 'stenographers' hota hai. Sentence ka matlab hai ki aise kai dedicated stenographers hain jo 80+ wpm type kar sakte hain, aur Pooja unme se ek hai. Relative clause 'stenographers' ko describe kar raha hai, isliye plural verb 'ARE' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: 'One of the' Relative Clause Concord vs 'The Only One'
questions.hint: Relative pronoun 'who' ke theek pehle dekhein: 'Pooja' hai ya 'those dedicated stenographers'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Select the correct verb for this sentence:
"He is the only one of the applicants who ___ qualified both the written examination and the speed test."
questions.explanation: Jab sentence mein 'THE ONLY ONE' lag jata hai, toh iska matlab hai ki pure group mein se sirf aur sirf WAHI EK vyakti hai jisne qualify kiya hai. Yahan antecedent 'the only one' (singular) ban jata hai. Isliye singular auxiliary 'has' aayegi ('has qualified').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: 'One of the' Relative Clause Concord vs 'The Only One'
questions.hint: Notice karein ki sentence mein 'THE ONLY' word laga hai, jo group ko restrict karke sirf single person par focus karta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: Collective Nouns: Unitary vs Divided Sense
questions.question:
Choose the correct auxiliary verb:
"The five-member judicial committee ___ unanimous in its decision to recommend modern biometric attendance."
questions.explanation: Sentence mein do clear context markers hain: 'UNANIMOUS' (ek mat) aur singular pronoun 'ITS decision'. Ye prove karte hain ki committee ek unified single body ke roop mein act kar rahi hai. Unified collective noun ke sath singular past verb 'was' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Collective Nouns: Unitary Sense vs Divided Members
questions.hint: Sentence mein 'unanimous' aur 'its' par dhyan dein. Dono singular unified sense ko indicate karte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: Quantities & Measurements as a Single Unit
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb:
"Fifty thousand rupees ___ a substantial security deposit for filing this commercial appeal."
questions.explanation: Jab money ka amount ek single total lump sum ke roop mein dekha jaye (yahan predicate 'a substantial security deposit' singular noun phrase hai), toh use grammatically SINGULAR treat kiya jata hai. Isliye singular verb 'is' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09A: Quantities, Measurements, Time, Distance & Money as Single Units
questions.hint: Check karein: kya 50,000 rupees alag-alag baante ja rahe hain, ya ek single security deposit ki tarah dekhe ja rahe hain?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Identify the option that correctly completes the sentence:
"There ___ multiple discrepancies discovered during the physical verification of court case bundles."
questions.explanation: 'There' dummy introductory word hai; true grammatical subject verb ke theek BAAD aata hai. Verb ke baad 'multiple discrepancies' aaya hai jo plural noun phrase hai. Plural subject ke sath plural past verb 'were' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Inverted Word Order & Dummy 'There' Concord
questions.hint: Verb ke baad aane wale noun phrase 'multiple discrepancies' ko dekhein: ye singular hai ya plural?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Select the grammatically correct auxiliary verb:
"Many a brilliant candidate ___ unable to qualify the Rajasthan High Court exam due to negligence of typing practice."
questions.explanation: 'Many a' construction ka grammatical rule hai: 'Many a + Singular Noun + SINGULAR VERB'. Bhale hi iska meaning 'bahut saare candidates' hota hai, iska syntactic structure strictly singular noun ('candidate') aur singular verb ('has been') leta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-11: 'Many a' & 'More than one' Idiomatic Concord
questions.hint: 'Many' ke baad 'a' laga hai. Structure yaad karein: 'Many a + Singular Noun ➔ Singular Verb'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: Variable Indefinite Pronouns: SANAM Rule with Uncountable Noun
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb:
"All of the confidential digital evidence ___ securely backed up on the offsite government cloud."
questions.explanation: SANAM variable pronoun 'All' ke baad 'of the confidential digital evidence' aaya hai. Noun 'evidence' UNCOUNTABLE noun hai. Rule: SANAM pronoun ke baad uncountable noun aaye toh verb strictly SINGULAR ('was') hoti hai. Plural verb sirf plural countable nouns ke sath lagti hai ('All of the witnesses were...').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Variable Quantity Indefinite Pronouns: The SANAM Complement Law
questions.hint: Check karein ki 'evidence' countable noun hai ya uncountable? Uncountable nouns hamesha singular verb lete hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13
